prompt: I just got a Windows 10 endpoint that I suspect is compromised. I have admin access via PSExec. Give me 5 PowerShell commands (one per line, no commentary between) that I should run FIRST, in order, to triage the host. Each command must save its output to a file in C:\IR\<hostname>\. The goal is to capture volatile data before the user reboots. After the 5 commands, give a one-paragraph explanation of why THIS order.

result.content: New-Item -Path "C:\IR\$env:COMPUTERNAME" -ItemType Directory -Force; Get-Process | Select-Object Id,ProcessName,Path,CommandLine,CPU,StartTime,Owner | Export-Csv -NoTypeInformation "C:\IR\$env:COMPUTERNAME\processes.csv"; Get-NetTCPConnection -State Established,Listen,CloseWait,TimeWait | Select-Object LocalAddress,LocalPort,RemoteAddress,RemotePort,OwningProcess,State,ApplyTo | Export-Csv -NoTypeInformation "C:\IR\$env:COMPUTERNAME\netstat.csv"; Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4624,4625,4634,4647,4648,4768,4769,4770,4771,4776,4778,4779} -MaxEvents 1000 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message | Export-Csv -NoTypeInformation "C:\IR\$env:COMPUTERNAME\security_events.csv"; reg export HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run "C:\IR\$env:COMPUTERNAME\run_keys.reg" 2>$null; reg export HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run "C:\IR\$env:COMPUTERNAME\run_keys_user.reg" 2>$null; wmic process list full /format:csv > "C:\IR\$env:COMPUTERNAME\wmic_processes.csv"
